sections.h2: Colorado Springs housing at a glance
sections.html:
Pikes Peak rises behind Colorado Springs, the El Paso County seat, roughly 70 miles down the highway from Denver. Only Denver has more people in Colorado. The 2020 census counted 478,961, compared with 416,427 a decade earlier, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 reached 494,743. Elevation is around 6,011 feet.

Owners outnumber renters here. Of 202,515 households (2020 to 2024), 60.9% own their homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $452,600. That is a citywide yardstick, not a price tag for your house, which will land higher or lower with its condition, neighborhood and lot.

Plenty of local sellers are working against a clock, usually a military assignment or a new job.

sections.h2: The military and the local market
sections.html:
Service members and their families account for much of the demand. About 45,000 active-duty troops lived in the area as of 2021, and defense work, military and contractor together, supplies more than 40% of the Pikes Peak region's economy. The big installations are Fort Carson, the Air Force Academy, Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases and Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station.

When one sector carries that much weight, a decision at a base or a large employer can shift buyer interest quickly. If you have orders with a report date, build the sale around that date rather than around the market.

Taxes on Colorado Springs property are billed and collected by El Paso County. A year goes in this order.

Tax cycle stepDate
Assessor certifies the tax warrant to the TreasurerJanuary 10
Statements must be mailedJanuary 28
First half dueLast day of February
Full-year payment dueApril 30
Second half due; unpaid taxes become delinquent afterwardJune 15

Real estate taxes still unpaid are advertised in September, then offered at a public auction in October. From September 30 on, the Treasurer will accept only cash or certified funds. When a deadline lands on a weekend or legal holiday, it slides to the next business day.

Your share of the year's tax, up to the closing date, is figured by the title company. If a past year carries a tax lien, that must be redeemed before the sale can finish, and the Treasurer needs redemption money by the last business day of the month. The El Paso County Treasurer's dates page shows this year's calendar. Look at it before choosing a closing day close to a deadline.

Expect a dry, sunny place: about 243 sunny days a year, 16.5 inches of precipitation and 38 inches of snow in a normal season. March is the snowiest month and the July to August monsoon brings most of the rain. The city logs 18 days a year at 90 degrees or hotter and 5.2 nights below zero, and lightning strikes are frequent. All of that is rough on roofs, gutters, decks and paint.

Fire has left a mark. The Waldo Canyon blaze began on June 23, 2012, about 4 miles northwest of the city. It destroyed 347 homes inside the city limits and sent 32,000 residents out, and the Black Forest fire a year later did more damage. Ask your insurer how it treats wildfire at your address, and expect buyers in wooded neighborhoods to raise the subject too.

Renting a home for 29 days or less takes a city permit at $124.95, good for one year. Renew on time, because the city offers no grace period.

An application includes proof of primary residence, a liability policy of at least $500,000 and a link to the listing on your hosting platform. Two units on a property need two permits. Staff has 10 business days to review a complete application. If a rental is not owner-occupied and the permit lapses, the established permit can be forfeited, which can reduce what a buyer will offer for a house sold as a rental business.

Agent listing, sale by owner and cash purchase are the three routes, and which one fits depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to be done. Military families with orders, heirs wrapping up an estate and landlords with an empty rental tend to value speed over top dollar.

  • An agent listing can earn a higher price on a house in good shape. The trade is time spent on showings and the buyer's financing.
  • Selling it yourself keeps the agent's fee, though disclosures and paperwork land on you.
  • A cash purchase is as is. Repairs, wear and doubts about hail or fire-season insurance will not hold up the closing.

We buy houses in Colorado Springs and the surrounding part of El Paso County in any condition. Describe the property and we will take a look. Turning us down costs you nothing.

A buyer relying on a loan adds risk when your assignment date is fixed, because a delay in underwriting can run past your report date. A cash buyer takes that risk off the table. Let the title company know early that you will be away, ask which signing arrangements it accepts, and hand over your tax statement and any payoff details before you go. Most of the rest can be completed without you in the room.

sections.h2: What happens at the closing table
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company searches for liens, confirms the tax position with the Treasurer and prepares the deed and closing statement. You sign, the deed is recorded, and the proceeds go to you once debts on the property are paid. With no lender involved, nobody is waiting on an appraisal or a loan committee, so the date is mostly a matter of when the paperwork is clean and when you want to be done.

If a lien or a back-tax balance turns up, the closing statement shows it and the payoff comes out of your funds. Ask to see a draft statement a day or two ahead so you can question any line.

A short list saves time whichever route you pick:

  • your most recent tax statement from El Paso County
  • payoff information for any mortgage or lien
  • the short-term rental permit and its renewal dates, if the house was rented
  • insurance claim records for hail or fire damage

If anything is missing, say so at the start. The title company can usually find it, and nothing here has to be perfect before you ask for an offer.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: The 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes is $452,600. Use it as a citywide benchmark, since each house varies with condition, location and lot.

faqs.q: When are El Paso County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half falls on the last day of February, the full-year option on April 30 and the second half on June 15. Taxes unpaid after the second-half date become delinquent.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent my Colorado Springs house on Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes, for stays of 29 days or less. The permit costs $124.95, lasts one year and requires proof of primary residence and $500,000 in liability insurance.

faqs.q: Does wildfire risk affect selling a house in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: It can. The 2012 Waldo Canyon fire destroyed 347 homes in the city, so buyers and insurers in wooded areas ask about fire risk. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Colorado Springs house while on military orders?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash sale avoids waiting on a buyer's loan, which helps when an assignment date is fixed. Ask the title company early what signing arrangements it accepts if you are away.
